title: 2015 AMC 12B Problem 3
statement: Isaac has written down one integer two times and another integer three times. The sum of the five numbers is \(100,\) and one of the numbers is \(28.\) What is the other number?

solutions.text:
Write \(2x + 3y = 100.\) If \(28\) were written twice, then \(3y = 100 - 56 = 44,\) which is not a multiple of \(3.\)

So \(28\) is written three times: \(2x = 100 - 84 = 16,\) giving \(x = 8.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let \(x\) appear twice and \(y\) appear three times, so \(2x + 3y = 100\)
Test whether \(28\) is the number written two times or three times, and keep the integer case
